eraseDevice.title: Erase This Device
eraseDevice.subtitle: Delete everything Vela stored here
eraseDevice.desc: Everything Vela stored on this device is deleted. No backup, no undo.
eraseDevice.loses: You lose: transaction history, contacts and groups, browsing history, dApp permissions, custom tokens and networks, endpoint settings and every preference.
eraseDevice.keeps: You keep the wallet: its passkeys are with your passkey provider, not this app — sign in again and the same address returns. Not erased: Vela Relay keeps sent transactions up to 14 days, the key index keeps registrations up to 30 days, and the public-key record on chain is permanent; no one can delete it.
eraseDevice.failed: The erase did not finish. Some data is still on this device and you are still signed in — try again.

welcome.tagline:
Your keys, your coins.
Simple as a tap.
welcome.featureNoMnemonicBody: Create and sign in with a passkey on your device — no 12 words to copy down and guard.
welcome.featureOneAddressBody: The same address works on every supported network, and you can add your own.
welcome.featureOpenSourceBody: The app and backend services are open source — you can run a stack that is entirely your own.
welcome.featureKeyCustodyTitle: Keys live in your password manager
welcome.featureKeyCustodyBody: Passkeys are kept by Apple Passwords or Google Password Manager — Vela never touches them.
welcome.featureSafeContractBody: Accounts are built on audited Safe contracts, not a custom implementation.
welcome.featureStablecoinGasBody: Most networks let you pay fees in stablecoins — no need to hold the native coin first.
welcome.heroTitle:
An Ethereum wallet
you actually own
welcome.heroSubtitle: Signing is done on your device. Your passkey’s private key never goes to Vela.

intro.noSeedBody: Create your wallet with this device's fingerprint or face. No twelve words to write on paper, hide in a drawer, and fail to find one day.
intro.custodyBody: Your passkeys live where you keep them: this device's password manager, or a hardware security key. Vela can't reach them, and can't spend for you.
intro.chainsBody: The same address works on 24 networks, and fees can be paid in stablecoins — no stocking up on a native coin for each one.

meta.title: Vela Wallet — the passkey wallet
meta.description: A passkey wallet with no seed phrase: one address across 24 networks, audited Safe v1.4.1 contracts, stablecoin gas, fully open source and self-hostable.

treasuryBootstrap.title: Start this network's relayer
treasuryBootstrap.lead: This network's relayer treasury is low on gas. Fund it to resume sending.
treasuryBootstrap.disclaimer: Non-refundable. This gas goes to the bundler operator (not Vela), to start this network's relayer — it does not pay for your transaction.
treasuryBootstrap.operatorLead: Vela's operator runs this network's relayer, and it is out of gas. Telling them is the fastest fix — and it stays fixed for everyone.
treasuryBootstrap.customLead: You added this network, so Vela's operator may have no way to hold gas on it — a local or private chain is nobody else's to fund. Starting its relayer is up to you.
treasuryBootstrap.watching: Checking every few seconds — closes by itself once funded.
treasuryBootstrap.qrLabel: Scan to send from another wallet

relayUnreachable.title: The relay can't reach this network
relayUnreachable.operatorLead: Vela's relay can't reach this network right now. It's the operator's to fix — telling them is the fastest way.
relayUnreachable.customLead: You added this network, and the relay can't reach it. The relay reads it through the RPC you set, so that RPC must be a public https address — a node on your own computer or network needs a relay running beside it.
relayUnreachable.settingsHint: Change the network's RPC, or set Settings → Service endpoints → Vela Relay to one that reaches it.

backup.title: Copy this wallet's record to Ethereum
backup.couldNotCheck: Couldn't check. Tap to try again.
backup.cannotCopy: This older wallet can't be copied
backup.explain: Your wallet's record on Gnosis is public: its address and name, and for each key its name, public key, credential ID and authenticator model. A device with one of your passkeys finds this wallet through it. This puts a copy on Ethereum too. It's one Ethereum transaction: you confirm it with a passkey and pay its network fee in a coin you hold on Ethereum. The copy can't move money or bring back a lost passkey.
